answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost. A wharf stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a pigment holds the rep...
